_note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Himadri Speciality Chemical (consolidated, Rs crore). Three business lines: (1) core carbon materials and chemicals (coal tar pitch, carbon black incl. speciality, naphthalene, oils, SNF, new speciality chemicals) plus the captive power plant's external sales; (2) Others: Birla Tyres and mining; (3) new energy materials (LFP cathode, anode). EBITDA follows the company definition (before forex and other income); history from Screener is after forex (FY26 forex loss Rs 43.6 cr), so the Excel reconciliation row shows the forex. We assume no forex gains or losses. Valued on P/E on Sep-28E EPS.

segments.name: Carbon materials & chemicals (incl. captive power)
segments._why: Volume x realisation. Standalone volume 564 kt in FY26 (+2%); Q1FY27 132 kt (-6% YoY) but realisation ~Rs 96,600/t (+23%) as higher raw-material costs after the West Asia crisis were passed on. Capacity was ~80% used in Q1 with 90%+ expected in FY27 (new 70 kt speciality black line at 85-90%, distillation debottlenecked to 600 kt, liquid-pitch exports, anthraquinone/carbazole from Q2FY27). We assume volume +6% / +8% / +5% (600 / 648 / 680 kt) and realisation +11% / -2% / +2% (prices ease from Q1's peak): revenue +17% / +6% / +7%. Q1FY27 core revenue was +15% YoY.
segments._marginWhy: Core EBITDA per tonne (consolidated core EBITDA / standalone volume): Rs 4,400 FY22, Rs 13,400 FY24, Rs 15,300 FY25, Rs 17,300 FY26, ~Rs 23,700 in Q1FY27 (helped by price rises and the new speciality line). We assume Rs 20,500 / 21,000 / 21,500 per tonne (FY27E-29E), i.e. Q2-Q4FY27 back to ~Rs 19,600 as raw-material prices settle, then mix gains from SSCB, CNT and anthraquinone. That is a 24.0% / 25.0% / 25.1% margin on our revenue (FY26 22.3%, Q1FY27 24.2%).

segments.name: Others: Birla Tyres and mining
segments._why: Others segment revenue Rs 274 cr in FY26 (Birla Tyres Rs 187 cr from the May-2025 restart; the rest mining). Q1FY27 Rs 144 cr (tyres ~Rs 127 cr), with mining stopped pending an environmental clearance (3-6 months). Management targets Rs 3,000 cr of tyre revenue in 4-5 years. We assume tyres ~Rs 590 cr in FY27 (quarterly sales rising from Rs 127 cr to ~Rs 170 cr) plus a little mining in H2: Rs 620 cr; then +66% and +45% (Rs 1,030 cr and Rs 1,490 cr), about half of management's path by FY29.
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA Rs 27.9 cr in FY26 (10%), mostly mining profit (Q4FY26 EBIT Rs 25.4 cr); Q1FY27 EBIT Rs 1.2 cr with no mining. Management expects tyre EBITDA break-even in FY27. We assume 2% / 5% / 7%: a sub-scale tyre maker with a revived brand, well below the 12-15% of established tyre companies.

segments.name: New energy materials (LFP cathode, anode)
segments._why: No battery-material revenue in FY26 (the base of Rs 1 cr is notional: the engine needs a non-zero base). Anode: 200 tpa plant from Apr-2026, revenue potential Rs 120-130 cr, samples at stage B of four (approval takes 1.5-2 years). LFP: 2,000 tpa in Q3FY27, Phase 1 of 40,000 tpa built over the following ~12 months, FY29 the first full year; ~Rs 3,000 cr revenue at full use (~Rs 7.5 lakh/t). We assume Rs 20 cr in FY27, Rs 350 cr in FY28 (~4,000 t of LFP plus anode samples) and Rs 1,000 cr in FY29 (~12,000 t, 30% of Phase 1): customer approvals and Chinese price parity are the constraints.
segments._marginWhy: Start-up losses in FY27 (about -Rs 25 cr on two small plants), break-even-ish in FY28 (-3%) and 8% in FY29. Management prices at par with China and says it has a cost edge but discloses no margins; an analyst on the Q1 call calculated a negative spread at Chinese prices. Chinese LFP makers have earned thin margins in the price war.

_unallocLabel: Forex loss/(gain) booked in other expenses (forecast: none)
_unallocWhy: History: Screener EBITDA is after forex (FY26 loss Rs 43.6 cr; Q1FY27 loss Rs 25.2 cr from hedges). Management says no further forex hit after Q1 and keeps positions open as imports and exports roughly match. Forecast: zero.
_capexWhy: Management (Q1FY27 call): ~Rs 2,000 cr of announced capex (LFP Rs 1,125 cr, CNT Rs 70 cr, SSCB Rs 170 cr, other speciality chemicals, ~Rs 500 cr Birla Tyres modernisation/OTR conversion), ~Rs 1,000 cr in FY27 and ~Rs 1,000 cr in FY28, self-funded. FY29 Rs 700 cr: maintenance (~Rs 150 cr), the PCR tyre plant and an anode scale-up that is not yet announced. FY26 capex was Rs 450 cr.
_depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs 68 cr on a gross block of ~Rs 2,600 cr (2.6%); Q1FY27 Rs 21 cr. The model adds capex to gross block at once (CWIP held flat at Rs 372 cr), so 3% gives ~Rs 100 cr in FY27 rising to ~Rs 155 cr in FY29 as the LFP plant is capitalised.
_treasuryWhy: Other income entered directly (below); no yield on the model's cash line.
_otherIncomeWhy: FY26 Rs 171 cr included a Rs 100 cr fair-value gain on investments (IBC, Sicona etc.) and Rs 44 cr of deposit interest; Q1FY27 Rs 56 cr. We assume Rs 150 cr in FY27 (Q1 plus ~Rs 31 cr a quarter) and Rs 110 cr after: deposit and fund income on a shrinking cash pile as Rs 2,000 cr of capex is spent; no further fair-value gains.
_interestWhy: FY26 Rs 64 cr; Q1FY27 Rs 22 cr. Borrowings (Rs 770 cr at Mar-26) are mostly short-term lines and commercial paper parked in deposits; management plans no new debt for capex.
_payoutWhy: Rs 0.80 a share for FY26 (~5% of EPS); cash goes to capex.

dcf._betaWhy: Commodity-linked feedstock and customers (aluminium, tyres, electrodes) and an early-stage battery business, but net cash: beta 1.0, cost of equity 12.5%. With almost no net debt the cost of equity is the WACC.
dcf._tgWhy: Nominal growth of ~5.5%: aluminium, tyres and construction track Indian GDP; battery materials faster; coal tar supply is tied to steel output.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from the FY29 battery ramp to 8% by FY38.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from ~8% of revenue (FY29E) to 4.5% (maintenance plus modest growth).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: EBITDA per tonne holds near Q1FY27's level as speciality black, SSCB, CNT and anthraquinone lift the mix; Birla Tyres follows management's path; LFP approvals arrive on time.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Raw-material prices fall and EBITDA per tonne slips back towards FY26's ~Rs 17,000; tyres stay sub-scale; LFP approvals slip a year and the plants run at a loss.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: P/E on Sep-28E EPS (half FY28E, half FY29E). The only institutional broker, ICICI Securities, uses a sum of the parts with the core on FY28E EV/EBITDA; for a company with net cash and little interest that carries the same information as P/E, its other parts are not public, management guides on profit (Rs 1,100 cr+ PAT in FY28) and retail brokers use P/E. 25x = HSCL's one-year-forward P/E median since Apr-2021 (24.9x, no trough years excluded). No sector cut: listed chemicals trade ~28% below their five-year medians, but HSCL's median already includes 2021-23 at 8-13x, when peers were at their richest. Growth (our EPS +15% a year FY26-29E) and returns (ROE ~16-17% vs a 12.5% cost of equity, negative free cash flow in FY27-28E) do not justify a premium.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Close to ICICI Securities' method for the core business: 15x FY28E EV/EBITDA in Apr-2026 (12x in Jan-2026). HSCL's own trailing EV/EBITDA median since 2021 is ~23x, ~17x one year forward at our EBITDA growth. 16x Sep-28E EBITDA plus net cash and investments at Sep-27E (model basis).

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 12-year FCFF at 12.5% (cost of equity = WACC with net cash), terminal growth 5.5%; working capital held at the FY26 ratio of revenue (~29%).
